beads.greek: [3.5.11] Supra zophorum denticulus est faciendus tam altus quam epistylii media fascia; proiectura eius quantum altitudo.
beads.english: [3.5.11] Above the frieze the dentil is to be made as high as the middle fascia of the architrave; its projection is to be as much as its height.

beads.greek: intersectio, quae graece μετόπη dicitur, sic est dividenda, uti denticulus altitudinis suae dimidiam partem habeat in fronte, cavus autem intersectionis huius frontis e tribus duas partes; huius cymatium altitudinis eius sextam partem.
beads.english: The interspace (intersectio), which in Greek is called μετόπη, is to be divided thus: the dentil is to have on its front half of its height, and the hollow (cavus) of this interspace two parts out of three of this front; its cymatium is to be a sixth part of its height.

beads.greek: corona cum suo cymatio, praeter simam, quantum media fascia epistylii; proiectura coronae cum denticulo facienda est, quantum erit altitudo a zophoro ad summum coronae cymatium; et omnino omnes ecphorae venustiorem habeant speciem, quae quantum altitudinis tantundem habent proiecturae.
beads.english: The cornice with its cymatium, apart from the sima, is to be as much as the middle fascia of the architrave; the projection of the cornice together with the dentil is to be made as much as the height from the frieze to the top cymatium of the cornice; and in general all projections (ecphorae) have a more graceful appearance which have as much projection as they have height.

beads.greek: [3.5.12] Tympani autem, quod est in fastigio, altitudo sic est facienda, uti frons coronae ab extremis cymatiis tota dimetiatur in partes novem et ex eis una pars in medio cacumini tympani constituatur, dum contra epistylia columnarumque hypotrachelia ad perpendiculum respondeant.
beads.english: [3.5.12] The height of the tympanum, which is in the pediment, is to be made thus: the whole front of the cornice, from the outermost cymatia, is to be measured off into nine parts, and of these one part is to be set up in the middle as the apex of the tympanum, provided that it answers plumb to the architraves and the hypotrachelia of the columns below.

beads.greek: coronaeque supra aequaliter imis praeter simas sunt conlocandae.
beads.english: And the upper cornices are to be set equal to the lower ones, apart from the simae.

beads.greek: insuper coronas simae, quas Graeci ἐπαιετίδες dicunt, faciendae sunt altiores octava parte coronarum altitudinis.
beads.english: Above the cornices the simae, which the Greeks call ἐπαιετίδες, are to be made higher than the cornices by an eighth part of the cornices' height.

beads.greek: acroteria angularia tam alta, quantum est tympanum medium, mediana altiora octava parte quam angularia.
beads.english: The corner acroteria are to be as high as the tympanum is at its middle; the middle ones an eighth part higher than the corner ones.

english_sentences: [3.5.11] Above the frieze the dentil is to be made as high as the middle fascia of the architrave; its projection is to be as much as its height.

And the upper cornices are to be set equal to the lower ones, apart from the simae.
Above the cornices the simae, which the Greeks call ἐπαιετίδες, are to be made higher than the cornices by an eighth part of the cornices' height.
The corner acroteria are to be as high as the tympanum is at its middle; the middle ones an eighth part higher than the corner ones.

beads.greek: [3.5.13] Membra omnia, quae supra capitula columnarum sunt futura, id est epistylia, zophora, coronae, tympana, fastigia, acroteria, inclinanda sunt in fronte suae cuiusque altitudinis parte XII , ideo quod, cum steterimus contra frontes, ab oculo lineae duae si extensae fuerint et una tetigerit imam operis partem, altera summam, quae summam tetigerit, longior fiet.
beads.english: [3.5.13] All the members which are to be above the capitals of the columns, that is, architraves, friezes, cornices, tympana, pediments, acroteria, are to be inclined forward on the front by a twelfth part of their own respective height. The reason is that when we stand facing the fronts, if two lines are extended from the eye, and one touches the lowest part of the work and the other the highest, the one which touches the highest will be the longer.

beads.greek: ita quo longior visus linea in superiorem partem procedit, resupinatam facit eius speciem.
beads.english: Thus, the longer the line of sight runs toward the upper part, the more it makes that part appear to lean backward.

beads.greek: cum autem, uti supra scriptum est, in fronte inclinata fuerint, tunc in aspectu videbuntur esse ad perpendiculum et normam.
beads.english: But when, as has been written above, they have been inclined forward on the front, then to the view they will appear to be true to the perpendicular and the set-square.

beads.greek: [3.5.14] Columnarum striae faciendae sunt XXIIII ita excavatae, uti norma in cavo striae cum fuerit coniecta, circumacta anconibus angulos striarum dextra ac sinistra tangat cacumenque normae circum rotundationem tangendo pervagari possit.
beads.english: [3.5.14] The flutings of the columns are to be made twenty-four in number, hollowed out in such a way that when a set-square has been placed in the hollow of a fluting and turned about, it touches with its arms the edges of the flutings on the right and on the left, and the point of the set-square can travel round, touching the curvature throughout.

beads.greek: crassitudines striarum faciendae sunt, quantum adiectio in media columna ex descriptione invenietur.
beads.english: The thicknesses of the flutings are to be made as great as the addition in the middle of the column will be found to be from the diagram.

greek_sentences: [3.5.13] Membra omnia, quae supra capitula columnarum sunt futura, id est epistylia, zophora, coronae, tympana, fastigia, acroteria, inclinanda sunt in fronte suae cuiusque altitudinis parte XII , ideo quod, cum steterimus contra frontes, ab oculo lineae duae si extensae fuerint et una tetigerit imam operis partem, altera summam, quae summam tetigerit, longior fiet.
ita quo longior visus linea in superiorem partem procedit, resupinatam facit eius speciem.
cum autem, uti supra scriptum est, in fronte inclinata fuerint, tunc in aspectu videbuntur esse ad perpendiculum et normam.

[3.5.14] Columnarum striae faciendae sunt XXIIII ita excavatae, uti norma in cavo striae cum fuerit coniecta, circumacta anconibus angulos striarum dextra ac sinistra tangat cacumenque normae circum rotundationem tangendo pervagari possit.
crassitudines striarum faciendae sunt, quantum adiectio in media columna ex descriptione invenietur.
english_sentences: [3.5.13] All the members which are to be above the capitals of the columns, that is, architraves, friezes, cornices, tympana, pediments, acroteria, are to be inclined forward on the front by a twelfth part of their own respective height.

The reason is that when we stand facing the fronts, if two lines are extended from the eye, and one touches the lowest part of the work and the other the highest, the one which touches the highest will be the longer.
Thus, the longer the line of sight runs toward the upper part, the more it makes that part appear to lean backward.
But when, as has been written above, they have been inclined forward on the front, then to the view they will appear to be true to the perpendicular and the set-square.

[3.5.14] The flutings of the columns are to be made twenty-four in number, hollowed out in such a way that when a set-square has been placed in the hollow of a fluting and turned about, it touches with its arms the edges of the flutings on the right and on the left, and the point of the set-square can travel round, touching the curvature throughout.
The thicknesses of the flutings are to be made as great as the addition in the middle of the column will be found to be from the diagram.

beads.greek: [3.5.15] In simis, quae supra coronam in lateribus sunt aedium, capita leonina sunt scalpenda, disposita ita , uti contra columnas singulas primum sint designata, cetera aequali modo disposita, uti singula singulis mediis tegulis respondeant.
beads.english: [3.5.15] On the simae, which are above the cornice on the sides of temples, lions' heads are to be carved, arranged in such a way that first they are marked out opposite the individual columns, and the rest are arranged at equal intervals, so that each corresponds to the middle of each tile.

beads.greek: haec autem, quae erunt contra columnas, perterebrata sint ad canalem, qui excipit e tegulis aquam caelestem; mediana autem sint solida, uti, quae cadit vis aquae per tegulas in canalem, ne deiciatur per intercolumnia neque transeuntes perfundat, sed quae sunt contra columnas, videantur emittere vomentia ructus aquarum ex ore.
beads.english: Those, moreover, which will be opposite the columns are to be bored through to the channel that receives the rainwater from the tiles; but the middle ones are to be solid, so that the force of water that falls through the tiles into the channel may not be thrown down through the intercolumniations nor drench those passing by, while those that are opposite the columns may appear to emit, vomiting, belchings of water from the mouth.

beads.greek: Aedium ionicarum, quam apertissime potui, dispositiones hoc volumine scripsi; doricarum autem et corinthiarum quae sint proportiones, insequenti libro explicabo.
beads.english: I have written in this volume, as clearly as I could, the arrangements of Ionic temples; what the proportions of Doric and Corinthian temples are I shall explain in the following book.
